text:
fiona: quick gut-check: instead of a daemonset/cache agent we could use an eBPF-based in-VPC redirector that routes control-plane reads to a local kernel cache (no sidecars). thoughts?
amir: interesting. pro: zero-app-surface change, transparently accelerates reads for all pods. con: kernel-level ops, upgrade/compat matrix, and customers may resist eBPF for compliance.
cheng: also: how would invalidation work? kernel cache needs userland agent or control socket to apply invalidations. we could run a tiny userland updater (single binary) instead of full daemonset.
fiona: idea: single userland updater + eBPF redirector. bootstrap over PrivateLink to seed snapshot and exchange certs, then outbound-only mTLS for invalidations. avoids inbound peering.
amir: security: eBPF must be restricted (CAP_SYS_ADMIN?) and we need strong signing for the updater binary. BYOK customers will want KMS integration for assertions.
cheng: failure modes: if updater loses contact, kernel might serve stale certs. fallback: redirector consults userland via local AF_UNIX; if no response, fail-closed for HIGH-sensitivity ops, fail-open for LOW.
fiona: metrics: kernel_cache_hit, invalidation_latency_ms, updater_heartbeat, staleness_seconds, bootstrap_success. ops must have dashboards before pilot.
ops-bot: ticket RED-NTW-811 created for eBPF-redirector prototype; owners <@fiona> <@cheng>.
amir: compatibility matrix: maintainers must verify supported distro/kernel list. plan: start with Amazon Linux 2, Ubuntu 22.04. doc the kernel versions.
cheng: rollout plan: 1) internal sandbox with eBPF on controlled images, 2) partner pilot with opt-in, 3) wider availability as an opt-in feature. make default remain PrivateLink.
fiona: decision (tentative): prototype eBPF redirector + tiny userland updater seeded via a one-time PrivateLink bootstrap. opt-in only, BYOK optional, tombstone/invalidation via outbound mTLS, kernel compatibility gated. I'll draft RFC with sequence diagram and upgrade constraints. add anything I missed here.
